The image shows a sugarcane leaf with the following key features:

- **Affected part**: Leaf blade
- **Color pattern**: Pale yellowish-green/cream coloration running along the length of the leaf, with the central midrib area and large portions of the lamina showing chlorotic (yellowing/whitening) streaks
- **Texture**: The discoloration appears as broad, longitudinal pale streaks or bands along the leaf
- **Additional details**: Some small brownish lesions are visible near the edges, but the dominant feature is the elongated pale/yellow streaking pattern along the leaf axis
- **Pattern type**: Longitudinal striping/streaking, not mosaic patchy pattern, not circular spots

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: Causes narrow yellow/white streaks along the leaf veins — this matches well with the longitudinal pale streaking visible
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Typically shows mosaic (irregular patches), not uniform longitudinal streaks
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Primarily affects the midrib (yellowing of the midrib and lower leaf), but the whole lamina here looks affected
- **Leaf_Scald**: Typically shows scalded/water-soaked margins and cream-colored stripes along leaf margins
- **Yellow_Spot**: Causes oval yellow spots, not longitudinal streaks
- **Brown_Spot**: Causes brown oval/elongated spots — not the dominant feature here

The broad, pale longitudinal streaking along the length of the leaf blade is most consistent with **Leaf_Scald** (which causes cream/pale water-soaked lesions running lengthwise along the leaf) or **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**. However, the very broad, uniform pale zone covering most of the leaf width with a slightly irregular margin is more characteristic of **Leaf_Scald**, which presents as cream-to-straw colored lengthwise stripes that can cover large portions of the leaf.
